readerContract.humanQuestion: People use the phrase type of AI for jobs, methods, information forms, operating patterns and future capability claims. What do these labels actually mean, and how can several be true of one product without forming one giant hierarchy?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: A nontechnical reader can explain the principal public AI labels, show how they relate without flattening unlike categories, distinguish current systems from disputed or hypothetical claims, and use the framework on a new everyday product.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No technical vocabulary, coding, mathematics or engineering knowledge is assumed. Ordinary encounters with recommendations, phone photo search, chat assistants and workplace presentations are enough.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: AI is a broad field. Public labels answer different questions about a system: how it was built, what job it performs, what forms of information it uses, whether it works through actions or the physical world, how broad its abilities are and how strong the evidence is.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A single travel-planning assistant can recognise information, rank options, generate a plan, use several information forms and work through permitted steps. Each label contributes one different fact about the same product.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A durable, scannable 101 textbook introduction and orientation chapter. It gives a complete core explanation and routes later mechanisms to their proper chapters rather than pretending orientation is mastery.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: Ohhh. These words were answering different questions. I can now explain what each one adds and I know which claims deserve a raised eyebrow.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: AI is the broad field. The labels people call types of AI often describe different properties, so one product can truthfully have several without one label containing all the others.
causalSequence: Start with the ordinary AI product and the result the reader sees.
Ask which question each public label answers: approach, job, information form, operating pattern, physical interaction or breadth claim.
Apply compatible labels to one worked product while keeping current, disputed and hypothetical evidence status visible.
Use the same questions on a different product and route each deeper mechanism to its later chapter.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A travel-planning assistant recognises details, ranks options, generates a plan, works with text and images and may use permitted tools through several steps.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A phone photo app finds pictures of a dog, groups them and creates a new collage; the reader identifies the distinct label families without assuming the app is AGI or agentic.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: When a product or presentation says type of AI, ask what exact fact the label supplies and which question it answers before accepting a capability claim.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Ali-authored Introduction; human-context opening; broad-field meaning; approach families; task families; cross-cutting information/action properties; breadth claims; history; worked synthesis; explain/draw/use check; Key Definitions; compact sources.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: The chapter follows one conversation and worked product rather than repeating identical definition cards. It omits the global Nerd-O-Meter and includes no CSS-drawn diagram.

analogyPlan.concept: several AI jobs in one service
analogyPlan.analogy: A video shop can classify films, rank likely choices and recommend one title.
analogyPlan.mapping: The clerk performs several distinct decision jobs in one service, just as an AI product may combine recognition, ranking and recommendation.
analogyPlan.faithfulMechanism: Each named job maps to a separate result family; the comparison does not claim a clerk works like a model.
analogyPlan.whySimpler: The familiar service makes distinct jobs visible without technical machinery.
analogyPlan.whyItImprovesUnderstanding: The reader can separate classification, ranking and recommendation before meeting the labels.
analogyPlan.transferCheck: The reader repeats the distinction on a streaming service without relying on the video-shop setting.

humourPlan.lessonJob: PowerPoint and Blockbuster humour make label confusion and distinct task jobs memorable; every joke remains attached to the exact explanation it serves.

systemSynthesis.endState: The reader can explain that AI labels answer different questions, apply several compatible labels to one product and separate current capability from disputed or hypothetical breadth claims.
systemSynthesis.drawPrompt: Draw AI as the broad field, then six question branches: approach, job, information forms, operating pattern, physical interaction and breadth/evidence claim. Put one familiar product beside every branch that applies.
systemSynthesis.explainBackPrompt: Explain to a friend why generative, multimodal and agentic are not three rungs on one ladder.
systemSynthesis.applicationPrompt: Classify a phone photo product that finds dog photos and creates a collage, stating what is known, unknown and not implied.

explanationArc.sharedStartingPoint: A familiar presentation contains many AI labels but does not explain which questions they answer.
explanationArc.curiosityGap: How can one product be generative, multimodal and agentic without those words meaning the same thing?
mechanismSequence: Different labels describe approach, job, information, operating pattern, physical interaction or breadth.
One product combines components and can therefore carry several compatible labels.
Evidence status distinguishes current systems from disputed AGI and hypothetical ASI.
explanationArc.earnedClick: The labels are not one ladder; they are answers to different questions about the same system.
explanationArc.smallLanding: The next time the words breed in PowerPoint, the reader can ask which question each label actually answers.
explanationArc.safetyBoundary: Do not infer reliability, truth, safety, autonomy or AGI from a label alone.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The chapter could again become a technically neat taxonomy that assumes vocabulary, loses Ali’s voice and makes the reader reconstruct the relationships.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: One complete Introduction + Chapter 1 with the global depth toggle removed, no CSS diagram, one continuous worked product and reasoned explain/draw/use checks.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: An unfamiliar nontechnical reader can explain the label families in her own words, apply them to a new product and identify current, disputed and hypothetical claims while recognising the sustained LAiDIES relationship.
